settings.title: Settings
settings.inviteBody: Share this code with a parent so they can see how you are doing.
settings.inviteParentBody: Send a link to a parent, an older brother or sister, or a tutor — anyone who helps you. They can only look; they cannot change anything.
settings.inviteParentHow: Read it out to them, or send it on WhatsApp. In Dagar they tap “I have a parent code” and enter it.

settings.inviteParentSees: They will see: lessons you finished, which topics you are getting, your streak and your badges.
settings.inviteParentPrivate: They will not see the questions you asked the tutor. That stays yours.

install.title: Add Dagar to your home screen
install.body: It opens like an app, with its own icon. No download needed.
install.iosSteps: Tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
install.androidSteps: Open your browser menu (⋮) and tap “Add to Home screen”.
install.launcherNote: Added it but can’t see it? Some phones put it in your app list instead of the home screen — search for Dagar there.
install.inAppBrowser: You’re in WhatsApp’s browser, which can’t add apps. Tap the menu and choose “Open in Chrome”, then try again.
install.alreadyInstalled: Dagar is already on your home screen.

parent.howToHelp: If you have ten minutes together, {concept} is the one worth sitting with.
parent.claimIsLearner: This account is a learner's. Ask a parent to use their own.
parent.claimSelf: That is your own code — ask a parent to enter it.
parent.lessonsMeaning: A lesson is a short reading with an example. Each one takes about ten minutes.
parent.practiceMeaning: Practice questions are how the topic sticks. Around five a day is a good rhythm.
parent.streakMeaning: Days in a row with some learning done. Streaks are about the habit, not the score.
parent.milestonesMeaning: Badges are earned automatically for real progress. They are worth saying out loud at home.
parent.conceptsMeaning: “Mastered” means they are getting it right consistently. “Getting there” means it is coming — most are right, a few still are not. “Keep practising” is not a fail; it is simply the next thing to work on.
parent.helpFocus: If you have ten minutes together, {concept} is the one worth sitting with. You do not need to teach it — ask them to explain it to you, and see where they get stuck.
parent.helpAllWell: Nothing needs fixing this week. Ask them to show you something they worked out — explaining it back is how it sticks.
parent.helpEncourage: Noticing out loud that they showed up is worth more than checking the answers. That is the part only you can do.
parent.linkIntro: This is a read-only view. You cannot change anything here, and it updates as they learn.
parent.linkRevoked: This link is no longer active.
parent.linkRevokedHelp: Ask your child to open Dagar, go to Settings, and share a new one.
parent.private1: The questions they asked the tutor. That conversation is theirs alone — it is where a learner admits they are stuck.

forParents.title: For parents
forParents.intro: Dagar is a maths tutor for Classes 6 to 8, following the NCERT syllabus. Your child uses it to learn; you get a simple weekly picture of how they are doing.
forParents.stepsTitle: How to connect to your child
forParents.step1: Your child opens Dagar, goes to Settings, and taps “Invite a parent”. A 6-character code appears on their screen.
forParents.step2: They read it out to you, or send it on WhatsApp. The code works for 3 days.
forParents.step3: You create your own Dagar account here — your email, your password. It is separate from your child's.
forParents.step4: You enter the code once. From then on you go straight to their summary whenever you sign in.
forParents.sees1: How many lessons and practice questions they finished this week
forParents.sees2: Which topics they have got, and which need more practice
forParents.sees3: Their day streak, so you know if they are keeping the habit
forParents.sees4: Badges they earned — the moments worth celebrating at home
forParents.private1: The questions they asked the Dagar tutor. That conversation is theirs alone — it is where a learner admits they are stuck.
forParents.readOnly: Your view is read-only. There is nothing you can change, undo or delete — you cannot affect their learning by tapping anything.
forParents.noCodeBody: Ask your child to open Dagar and go to Settings. They can either send you a link on WhatsApp — no account needed — or tap “Invite a parent” for a code. Either way it is one tap for them.
forParents.sharedPhoneBody: That works. Both accounts can live on the same phone — sign out from Settings to swap between your child's view and yours.
forParents.waysTitle: Two ways to see how they are doing
forParents.linkWay1: Your child opens Dagar, goes to Settings, and taps “Share your progress”.
forParents.linkWay2: They send you the link on WhatsApp. You tap it, and their week opens straight away.
forParents.linkWay3: No account, no password, nothing to install. Keep the link and open it whenever you like — it always shows the latest week.
forParents.codeWayWhy: Worth doing if more than one adult wants to check in, or if you would rather sign in than keep a link on your phone.

privacy.title: What we keep
privacy.intro: Dagar keeps a small amount of information so it can remember where you are in your learning. Here is all of it, in plain words.

account.title: Your account
account.email: The email address used to sign in.
account.grade: Your class — 6, 7 or 8 — so we show the right chapters.
account.language: Which language you chose to learn in.

learning.title: Your learning
learning.lessons: Which lessons you have opened and finished.
learning.answers: The answers you give in practice and quizzes, so we know what to help with.
learning.streak: Your daily goal, streak and badges.

tutor.title: Your questions to the tutor
tutor.questions: What you ask the tutor, and what it answers.
tutor.retention: These are kept for 90 days and then deleted. They are never put into reports.

promises.title: Three things we do not do
promises.thirdParty: We never share your information with anyone else. There is no advertising company, no tracking service, and no other business receiving any of it.
promises.noAds: There are no adverts in Dagar, and nothing here is used to sell you anything.
promises.free: Dagar is free. We do not ask for money, and we do not ask for payment details.

delete.title: Getting rid of it
delete.body: You can ask us to delete everything at any time, and we will. Tell the teacher or the adult who shared Dagar with you, and they will pass it on.

parents.title: For parents
parents.body: If you are a parent or guardian, you can see how your child is getting on through a weekly summary, without creating an account yourself. You can also ask us to delete your child's information at any time.

deleteAccount.title: Delete your account?
deleteAccount.body: This removes your account and everything in it — the lessons you have finished, your practice, your streak and your badges. It cannot be undone, and we cannot get it back for you afterwards.
deleteAccount.failed: Something went wrong on our side and nothing was deleted. Try again?

goodbye.title: Your account is deleted
goodbye.body: Everything we had is gone — your lessons, your practice, your streak and your badges.
goodbye.ask: If you have a moment, what made you leave? One tap, and it is not linked to you.
goodbye.thanks: Thank you — that helps us make it better for someone else.
